name: Ember Hollow
tagline: a warm editorial burn over cold ash
contrast_notes: accent on neutral-50 = 4.87:1 (AA body). accent_ink on accent = 4.88:1 (AA body). accent on neutral-0 = 3.82:1 — large text and UI chrome only, use neutral-100 for body on dark.

name: Lemnian Hollow
tagline: a cool sweep from mint to mauve over gunmetal
avoid: anything needing hierarchy from colour alone
contrast_notes: On Gunmetal: Fairy Dust 8.53:1 (AAA body), Cool Steel 4.49:1 (large text / UI only, a hair under AA), Lavender Grey 3.77:1, Dusty Mauve 3.32:1 — all three mid-tones are large-text-and-chrome only. The three mid-tones sit within 1.14–1.35:1 of each other, so they are effectively isoluminant and must never be the only thing distinguishing two elements. Fairy Dust is 1.45:1 on white and unusable as a light-surface text colour.

name: Larkspur Orchard
tagline: cream and meadow-green pierced by one cornflower blue
contrast_notes: On Drab Dark Brown (anchor): Ivory 11.34:1, Vanilla 9.39:1, Tea Green 7.58:1 (all AAA body), Celtic Blue 2.37:1 (fails — chrome/large-text only, and marginal even there). Ivory/Vanilla and Vanilla/Tea Green are both near-isoluminant at 1.21:1 and 1.24:1 — the cream-to-green run reads as one soft band, not three distinct steps.

name: Amber Tideline
tagline: a sunset burning down into near-black tide
contrast_notes: On Licorice (anchor): Earth Yellow 10.05:1 (AAA body), Persian Orange 6.76:1 (AA body), Taupe Gray 4.05:1 (large text / UI only), Delft Blue 1.63:1 (fails — Delft Blue sits almost as dark as the anchor itself). Persian Orange/Earth Yellow are near-isoluminant at 1.49:1 — the two warm swatches at the bright end read as one band, not two distinct steps.

name: Lupine Twilight
tagline: a violet bloom over near-black foliage
contrast_notes: On Eerie Black (anchor): Laurel Green 7.53:1 (AAA body), Camouflage Green 5.35:1 (AA body), Rhythm 3.80:1 (large text / UI only), Ebony 2.90:1 (fails). Rhythm/Camouflage Green sit at 1.41:1 — near-isoluminant, the purple and the mid green read as one step despite the hue jump.

name: Strawberry Bramble
tagline: sage leaves and tart red over dark kelp
contrast_notes: On Kelp (anchor): Whiskey 4.43:1 (large text / UI only), Willow Grove 2.46:1 (fails), Tamarillo 1.26:1 (fails, near-isoluminant with Kelp — the red and the anchor sit at nearly the same depth). Only Whiskey clears anything on this anchor; the kit has no swatch that clears AA body against Kelp.

name: Paprika Bazaar
tagline: paprika and honey fading into pale crumpet
contrast_notes: On Hot Paprika (anchor): Crumpet 4.81:1 (AA body), Biscuit 3.39:1 (large text / UI only), Honeycomb 2.87:1 (fails). Crumpet/Biscuit (1.42:1) and Biscuit/Honeycomb (1.18:1) are both near-isoluminant — the three warm neutrals read as one cream-to-tan wash rather than three steps.

name: Matcha Ceremony
tagline: bright matcha settling into pale bamboo
contrast_notes: On Forest Brew (anchor): Bamboo Beige 9.82:1, Tea Mist 9.07:1, Matcha Lime 7.41:1 — all three clear AAA body. Bamboo Beige/Tea Mist (1.08:1) and Tea Mist/Matcha Lime (1.22:1) are both near-isoluminant — the three light swatches read as one soft band and only separate from each other by hue, not lightness.

name: Basement Amethyst
tagline: a violet signal in concrete and sodium light
contrast_notes: accent_ink on accent = 5.02:1 (AA body), which is the number that matters: the accent is a button fill, not text. accent on neutral-50 = 4.72:1 (AA body). accent on neutral-0 = 3.90:1 — large text and UI chrome only, never accent-coloured body copy on dark. neutral-100 on neutral-0 = 16.38:1, neutral-700 on neutral-50 = 9.97:1. No single accent can be AA body on both a near-black and a near-white canvas; the two luminance windows do not overlap, so do not go looking for one. The semantics are tuned for the DARK canvas: info 7.19:1, success 10.43:1, warning 10.70:1, danger 7.05:1 on neutral-0. On the light canvas substitute info #2563EB (4.86:1), success #15803D (4.72:1), warning #B45309 (4.72:1), danger #B91C1C (6.08:1); the dark-tuned set measures 1.7-2.6:1 there and is unusable. warning and danger sit 39 degrees apart in hue at a 1.52:1 luminance ratio, so they must never be the only thing distinguishing two states.
